create.name: Amy Hollowell
create.bio:
Amy Hollowell is a Zen teacher and poet who grew up in Minneapolis and moved to France in 1981, where she has lived ever since; she now lives in Montreuil, just east of Paris. She trained with Catherine Genno Pagès Roshi and spent several years in the lay Zen community of Dana Sangha that the two helped to start. She received dharma transmission in 2004, placing her in the White Plum lineage that comes down from Taizan Maezumi Roshi, and was given the title Roshi in 2015. Alongside her practice she worked for many years as an editor at the International Herald Tribune in Paris and as a literary translator.

In 2004 she founded Wild Flower Zen Sangha, a non-monastic community with no robes and no walls, which now meets in Paris, online and in Portugal, where a sister association was set up in 2012. Her teaching centres on sitting where we are and including whatever arises in ordinary working and family life, using zazen, koan study and dharma talks. She gives talks in English and French, leads weekly Zoom sittings and a Saturday study group, and runs residential retreats in France and Portugal, some of which combine meditation with creative writing. She has published several collections of poetry.

courses.title: Wild Flower Zen Autumn Retreat in Coimbra
courses.description: A residential Zen retreat run by the sangha's Portuguese association at a religious guesthouse outside Coimbra. Days follow a traditional sesshin rhythm of sitting and walking meditation with dharma talks; meals are vegan and rooms are shared.

courses.title: Into the Turning: A winter meditation and writing retreat
courses.description: A week over New Year at Dechen Chöling, a Shambhala retreat centre near Limoges, joining a Zen retreat structure with group writing sessions, outdoor practice and one-to-one meetings with the teacher. No experience of meditation or writing is needed; it is taught in French with English translation on request.
courses.price: From €300 EUR (programme fee; accommodation and meals extra)

courses.title: Weekly Zen Meditation (online and in Paris)
courses.description: Regular sittings on Zoom on weekday mornings and a Thursday evening of meditation with a dharma talk, plus an in-person evening in Paris. The Zoom link is sent on request by email, and newcomers are given an introduction.
courses.price: From €5 EUR per session; membership €40 EUR per month

free_resources.title: Wild Flower Zen Sangha Dharma Talks (podcast)
free_resources.description: Recorded dharma talks from the sangha's Zoom evenings and retreats, most of them given by Amy Hollowell in English. Free to stream.

free_resources.title: Zenscribe
free_resources.description: Her online notebook of short reflections on practice, retreats and daily life in English and French, kept from 2006 to 2020; the archive stays online.

free_resources.title: What Is Zen?
free_resources.description: A short bilingual introduction from the sangha's website to what Zen practice is and how it can be brought into everyday life.

flags: Base: her teacher biography says she lives in Montreuil, on the eastern edge of Paris (her sangha meets at Passage Courtois, Paris 11e); city recorded as Montreuil.
The email info@wildflowerzen.org is the sangha's shared inbox, not a personal address.

Videos are from the Wild Flower Zen Sangha YouTube channel (the community she founded and leads), not a personal channel; each one picked has a description naming her as the speaker. Talks by Sensei Joa Scetbon on the same channel were left out.
Wild Flower Zen Sangha's Portuguese association (sanghazenpt.org) runs her retreats in Portugal; it and Dechen Chöling are not Spiritpedia listings, so they appear only as offerings.
Into the Turning at Dechen Chöling is taught in French with English translation on request; her Zoom dharma talks and podcast are mainly in English.
Possible related listings in this sprint: her teacher Catherine Genno Pagès Roshi (Montreuil) and her successor Sensei Joa Scetbon (Paris and Arles) were in the queue as separate leads.

Rule slip while researching: a status check on anchor.fm/wild-flower-zen followed a redirect to creators.spotify.com, whose robots.txt disallows that path; the page was not used and the podcast link is the Apple Podcasts page instead.
